title: Spectral routing: computational identity, causal credit and collision-aware rewrite
summary: A cross-pass synthesis centered on ThirdWay. Unlike a version-number ancestry, this pass records an explicit fusion: ThirdWay says it is the separate arm between GAx's modal/computational families and V25's route-local delayed credit. Later gates then explicitly fuse Kompressori's low-rank operator edits with CausalHorizon's propagated causal overlap. TransformerStudy is kept as a parallel controlled probe of algorithm/routing geometry rather than falsely labeled a descendant.

edges.why: ThirdWay explicitly defines itself as the separate fusion arm between V25's separated causal routes/delayed local credit and GAx's computational modes/context-dependent gain.
ThirdWay T4 explicitly brings Kompressori's low-rank experience-induced operator changes into its compatibility problem.
ThirdWay T4 explicitly uses CausalHorizon's propagated event-space overlap Omega as the coordinate for deciding whether locally useful edits collide.

motifs.title: The same answer can hide different computation
motifs.description: GAx Gate 4 makes two mechanisms observationally identical until a counterfactual breaks the cue correlation. ThirdWay promotes computational identity/continuation into the protected object. TransformerStudy independently probes whether task-conditioned residual interventions change downstream nonlinear routing rather than merely translating a vector. This is a recurring question, not an ancestry claim.

motifs.title: Routing, credit and rewrite are separate jobs
motifs.description: GAx supplies context-sensitive modal gain, V25 supplies route-local eligibility under delayed scalar consequence, ThirdWay transports identity/credit as coordinates move, and Kompressori plus CausalHorizon turn later writes into a causal collision problem.

motifs.title: Locally safe rewrites can accumulate global damage
motifs.description: ThirdWay T7A shows that shrinking every individually acceptable write below a local risk ceiling does not make the sequence safe. The recurring lesson matches the broader genealogy: state must carry enough history of previous changes for future compatibility decisions.
